One of the highlights of Saturnalia is the tradition of gift-giving. Martial describes the gift-giving tradition in Epigram XIV, The Presents Made to Guests at Feasts:

Now, while the knights and the lordly senators delight in the festive robe, and the cap of liberty is assumed by our Jupiter; and while the slave, as he rattles the dice-box, has no fear of the Aedile, seeing that the ponds are so nearly frozen, learn alternately what is allotted to the rich and to the poor. Let each make suitable presents to his friends. That these contributions of mine are follies and trifles, and even worse, who does not know? or who denies what is so evident? But what can I do better, Saturn, on these days of pleasure, which your son himself has consecrated to you in compensation for the heaven from which he ejected you?

The "festive robe" (the Synthesis) and "cap of liberty" (the Pileus) Martial mentions you may remember from part 1 on how to dress for Saturnalia..

Martial goes on to list almost every kind of gift imaginable -- he lists over 100 different types of gifts. Some of them are what we'd find in a modern day Christmas cracker (such as a tooth pick, a comb, or dice), whereas some are quite lavish (such as dishes inlaid with gold, a marble hermaphrodite, or even an ape). So no matter what your budget, you now have a multitude of ideas of what to get your friends and family.

The Xenia

If you're going to give someone a gift, don't forget to add a Xenia Epigram. Xenia or the singular Xenium is Latin for gifts, coming from the Greek ξένιον ‎(xénion), which is the concept of a host's hospitality towards strangers. In Latin, this works both ways -- a host may give a gift to his guests, or a guest may give gifts to his host. Don't fret if you're not good with words -- Martial wrote another entire epigram entitled Xenia in which he provides appropriate Xenia for different sorts of gifts.

For example, if you brought your Saturnalia host a bottle of Signine wine (section CXVI of Martial's Xenia), you may attach a Xenium that has something along the lines of this:

You may drink Signine wine, which astringes the relaxed bowels; but, that it may not affect you too much, let your draughts be moderate.

With this knowledge of the types of gifts to give and the appropriate Xenia to accompany them, you'll be known as a great gift-giver among your friends.
